questions.question: Define producer, consumer and decomposer, and give one savanna example of each. Explain why a mushroom is not a producer.
questions.expected_answer: Producer: makes its own food from inorganic substances using sunlight (photosynthesis), e.g. grass, acacia tree. Consumer: cannot make food and eats other organisms, e.g. impala, lion, baboon. Decomposer: feeds on dead organisms and waste, breaking them down into simple substances returned to the soil, water and air, e.g. soil bacteria, fungi. A mushroom has no chlorophyll and cannot photosynthesise; it absorbs food from dead matter, so it is a decomposer.

questions.question: Classify a kudu, a cheetah, a chacma baboon and a vulture as herbivore, carnivore or omnivore, justify each from diet, and say how teeth would support your answer for the kudu and cheetah.
questions.expected_answer: Kudu: herbivore, eats leaves and grass; broad flat ridged molars for grinding. Cheetah: carnivore (predator), hunts and eats antelope; long canines and shearing cheek teeth. Baboon: omnivore, eats fruit, roots, insects and small animals; mixed teeth. Vulture: carnivore, specifically a scavenger, eats the flesh of dead animals (not a decomposer).

questions.question: Explain what decomposers return to the environment and why an ecosystem could not survive without them. Distinguish a scavenger, a detritivore and a decomposer at a carcass.
questions.expected_answer: Decomposers return carbon dioxide to the air and mineral salts (nitrates, phosphates etc.) to the soil/water, which producers reuse; without them dead material and waste would pile up and nutrients would be locked away, so plants and then everything else would fail. Scavenger (vulture, hyena): a consumer that eats the dead animal's flesh. Detritivore (maggots, earthworms, dung beetles): eats and shreds fragments of dead material and dung. Decomposer (bacteria, fungi): chemically breaks the remaining material down to simple substances.
